items.stem: Why is issuing a SELECT statement inside a LOOP over an internal table usually a performance problem in ABAP?

options.text: It sends one database round trip per loop pass instead of a single set-based query
options.rationale: Correct: each pass crosses to the database server, so N passes cost N round trips; a single joined/array SELECT does the work in one.

options.text: SELECT is not allowed inside a LOOP and raises a syntax error
options.rationale: It is syntactically allowed; the issue is performance, not a syntax error.

options.text: Internal tables cannot be read while a SELECT is open
options.rationale: Internal tables can be read freely; this is not the reason.

options.text: The database automatically caches the result so the loop is always fast
options.rationale: No such guarantee exists; repeated round trips dominate the cost.

items.explanation: Correct: each pass crosses to the database server, so N passes cost N round trips; a single joined/array SELECT does the work in one.

items.stem: Which statements about internal table types in ABAP are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A hashed table gives near-constant-time access by its unique key
options.rationale: Correct: hashed tables use a hash of the unique key for fast single-row access.

options.text: A sorted table keeps its rows ordered by the table key as rows are inserted
options.rationale: Correct: a sorted table maintains key order automatically and supports binary search.

options.text: A standard table guarantees unique keys automatically
options.rationale: Standard tables allow duplicates; uniqueness is not enforced.

options.text: A hashed table can be read efficiently by a non-key field
options.rationale: Hashed access is only efficient by the full unique key, not by arbitrary fields.

items.explanation: Correct: hashed tables use a hash of the unique key for fast single-row access.; Correct: a sorted table maintains key order automatically and supports binary search.

items.stem: In the ABAP Dictionary, what is the primary role of a domain?

options.text: It defines the technical attributes (type, length, value range) reused by data elements
options.rationale: Correct: a domain holds the technical definition and optional value list that data elements reference.

options.text: It stores the business table rows at runtime
options.rationale: Rows are stored in transparent tables, not domains.

options.text: It is the screen layout for a selection screen
options.rationale: Screen layout is unrelated to a Dictionary domain.

options.text: It is a user authorisation object
options.rationale: Authorisation objects are separate security metadata, not domains.

items.explanation: Correct: a domain holds the technical definition and optional value list that data elements reference.
